subject: Confirming data-use assurance, deletion paths, and snapshot retention
messages:
From: Helen Cho <helen.cho@globepay.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: security@globepay.com
Date: 2026-12-13T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Request: written confirmation on 'no training' + deletion timeline

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for taking time to talk earlier. As part of our vendor security review I need a short written confirmation we can share with our InfoSec and Legal teams addressing the following points: 

1) A clear statement whether Redwood ever trains models on customer-supplied content (API requests, uploads, embeddings, transcripts) by default, and if there are any opt-in programs that would change that.
2) End-to-end deletion timeline for customer content after a deletion request: what is removed from live stores, caches (KV cache, inference caches), persistence (DB/S3 snapshots), and how backups or replication are handled?
3) Retention windows for: request payloads, logs (access/error/telemetry), model request metadata, and scheduled snapshots.
4) If you can provide the technical controls to support a 'no training' assertion (e.g., pipeline separation, explicit opt-in flag, logs showing training datasets are separate).
5) Any available audit artifacts (SOC 2 section, diagram, or an internal runbook) we can attach to our review.

We can redact anything that is sensitive on your side; the goal is evidence we can circulate internally. Also attaching our standard vendor questionnaire for context (we'll share it separately if needed).

Appreciate a reply by end of day tomorrow if possible.

Thanks,
Helen
Senior Manager, Vendor Security
GlobePay

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>

Cc: security@globepay.com, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, mina_haddad@redwood.ai

Subject: RE: Request: written confirmation on 'no training' + deletion timeline

Hi Helen — thanks for the clear list. Summary up top, details below.

Short answer (executive summary):
- Redwood does not use customer content to train or improve our public or private LLMs by default. Training on customer data is strictly opt-in and requires an explicit, auditable contract and opt-in flag.
- Deletion request flow removes data from live services within a short window and initiates a controlled purge from backups; full eradication from all copies (including nightlies/backups) can take up to 90 days depending on the persistence tier unless a faster contract clause is agreed.

Detailed notes (technical + operational):
1) Training usage: by default all customer request/response content is processed for inference only. We maintain a separation in our pipelines so that production inference logs are not fed into model training datasets. Any training program that would use customer data requires a formal opt-in: legal addendum, product flag, and an isolated ingestion pipeline that is traceable. 

2) Caches and ephemeral stores: KV caches and inference caches are ephemeral per-seat and per-request; they are not persisted into training stores. On a deletion request we clear the customer-specific KV entries and expire in-memory caches immediately; this usually completes within minutes to hours depending on active requests.

3) Live persistence (primary stores): primary request payloads and customer-stored artifacts (uploads, files) are soft-deleted immediately and physically purged from primary stores within 7–14 days by default (timeline depends on the deployment: Hosted defaults to 7 days, Dedicated customers can request a 24–72 hour purge SLA via contract).

4) Backups and snapshots: automated snapshots and backup retention are tiered. Default hosted snapshot retention is 90 days. Backups are immutable for the retention window; however we run a documented purge workflow for customer deletion requests: a soft-delete marker plus a scheduled purge job that targets snapshot catalogs and backup indexes. Purge across backups and third-party replication can take up to 90 days. We can also offer accelerated backup purges as part of an enterprise addendum.

5) Logs and telemetry: Personally identifiable request payloads are not stored in long-term telemetry. Access and error logs (used for billing/infra/debug) are retained for 30 days by default; aggregated telemetry/metrics are retained longer but are stripped of payload-level data. We also support an option to shorten log retention for Dedicated/Private customers.

6) Evidence and controls: we can provide:
  - Architecture diagram showing isolated training pipelines (redacted as needed)
  - The internal deletion runbook we use to track purge jobs (screenshot/PDF)
  - SOC 2 Type II controls that reference data handling and change management (we can mark the relevant sections)

I've attached our latest data handling playbook and a small retention matrix tailored for vendors. If it's helpful, Marcus (cc'd) can add one paragraph on KV cache lifecycle and Mina can provide the SOC controls pointer.

Next steps: if GlobePay needs a contract clause or a bespoke purge SLA we can route to Sales/Legal and produce an addendum. Otherwise I can assemble a single one-page attestation you can share internally. Which would you prefer?

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Phone: +1 415-555-0182

Subject: RE: Request: written confirmation on 'no training' + deletion timeline

Hi Helen — quick technical clarifications to back Vanessa's summary.

- KV cache behavior: the KV cache used for prefix caching and short-term context is per-request and shard-scoped; we do not persist KV cache blobs into long-term object storage. We rotate and zeroize cache shards on tenant delete operations; zeroization is triggered by the deletion pipeline and the raft of cache servers acknowledge zeroize before we return completion.

- Model training segregation: training data ingestion has an allowlist/ingest-gate. Production inference logs never reach the training namespace without the opt-in flag checked and an ingest token issued by Product/Legal. That gate is logged and audited.

- Backups: our S3-compatible snapshot system keeps a manifest; the purge job removes manifest entries and triggers lifecycle rules to expire underlying objects. Where clients have cross-region replication we coordinate with cloud partner ops to ensure purge propagation; this is why the worst-case 90-day window exists.

If you want a short technical attestation (one paragraph + one diagram) I can draft it and include the cache zeroization log sample (redacted).

Thanks,
Marcus
Staff Software Engineer, Inference Runtime
marcus_lin@redwood.ai
